Global commercial real estate services and investment firm headquartered in Chicago, listed on the NYSE (JLL). B2B brand, well known in the property industry but little consumer awareness.

Chinese cloud computing and AI infrastructure provider headquartered in Beijing, majority-backed by Kingsoft and Xiaomi. Listed on Nasdaq (KC) since 2020 and in Hong Kong since 2025. Revenue is in the low billions of US dollars. B2B infrastructure brand with little consumer visibility outside China.

Privately held New York real estate company led by Charles Kushner, developing and owning residential, office, retail and mixed-use property mainly in New York, New Jersey and the US Northeast and Southeast, with a large multifamily portfolio of tens of thousands of apartments. Revenue comes from rents, development and property sales. Family-owned and private. Name is publicly known mainly through the family's political connections; limited consumer brand presence, so sponsorship appetite is uncertain.

LeSports, the sports media and rights business that grew out of Chinese video platform LeEco (Letv), based in Beijing. It paid large sums for sports rights, including Premier League and other football and motorsport packages in China, and ran streaming, events and e-commerce. Raised about CN¥8.8 billion in 2017, but parent LeEco ran into severe financial distress from 2017 and the business shrank sharply. Once a high-profile sports brand in China; now much diminished.

Bermuda-based life and annuity reinsurer founded in 2019 by Martello Re, backed by Warburg Pincus and others, which provides reinsurance to life insurers and pension risk transfer, with a focus on long-term annuity and life blocks in the US, UK and Canada. Customers are insurance companies, not individuals. Raised over $1.2 billion in equity capital. Specialist B2B financial firm with no consumer brand awareness.

Namdar Realty Group, a privately held real estate investment and development firm based in Great Neck, New York, run by the Namdar family. It owns and manages commercial and residential property including large shopping centres and apartment buildings across the US, and also has interests in other sectors. Revenue is from rents and property sales; debt and equity funding have been large. Private, low public profile and no consumer brand.

Indian infrastructure investment trust (InvIT) based in New Delhi, sponsored by the National Highways Authority of India, which monetises operating national highway toll roads by pooling them into a trust. Investors, including large global pension and sovereign funds, buy units and earn income from toll collections. The funding figure shown is in Indian rupees. Government-linked infrastructure vehicle with no consumer brand awareness; it is a financial structure, not a typical sponsor.

NetEase Cloud Music is a Chinese online music streaming and social platform operated by NetEase, based in Beijing, known for its user comments, playlists and original music community. It earns from subscriptions, advertising, live streaming and sales of music-related products, and has hundreds of millions of registered users. Listed in Hong Kong (9899) since December 2021, majority-owned by NetEase. Well-known consumer app in China, a strong youth audience, but little awareness elsewhere.

NorthPark Center is a large enclosed shopping mall in Dallas, Texas, owned by Nancy Rogers and the Nasher family's real estate company, with roughly 2 million square feet of retail space and anchors such as Neiman Marcus and Nordstrom. It earns rent from retailers and restaurants. A major Dallas retail destination, privately held and a well-known local consumer landmark, though not a national brand.

PRO Unlimited is a San Francisco-based provider of contingent workforce and vendor management technology, including its Fieldglass-type platform for managing freelancers and contractors, serving large enterprises that outsource staffing. It earns software and managed service fees. Funded by a major investment from Insight Partners and others; around $1.16 billion raised, with the last round in 2021. B2B software and services, with little public brand awareness.

RXR Realty is a New York-based real estate owner, developer and investment manager, founded in 2007 with a large office, multifamily and mixed-use portfolio across the New York tri-state area, with tens of billions in assets under management. Revenue comes from rents, fees and development. Privately held, led by Scott Rechler, with large institutional investors. Well known in the New York property market, though not a consumer brand.

Sodexo is a French multinational food services and facilities management company, headquartered at Issy-les-Moulineaux near Paris, listed on Euronext Paris (SW). It runs catering, cleaning and on-site services for corporate, education, healthcare, government and sports and leisure clients, plus employee benefit vouchers (Pluxee, spun off in 2024). It employs about 420,000 people in around 45 countries, with revenue of roughly 23 billion euros. Already a major hospitality supplier at sporting venues; a B2B brand with some public recognition.

Transportadora de Gas del Peru (TGP) operates the pipeline system that carries natural gas and natural gas liquids from the Camisea fields in the Peruvian jungle to Lima and the coast. Customers are power generators, industry and gas distributors. The shown funding is $1.4 billion. Owners have included Pluspetrol, Hunt Oil, SK, Sonatrach and Tecpetrol through the Camisea consortium and Enagas as a shareholder. B2B energy infrastructure with little consumer visibility. Revenue comes from rent from corporate tenants. Founded as a REIT in the 1990s, it holds a portfolio of several million square feet. Mainly B2B; little consumer awareness beyond its local markets.

Aernnova Aerospace is a Spanish tier-one aerostructures supplier, headquartered in Miñano Mayor in Álava, Basque Country. It designs and manufactures wings, tail sections, fuselage parts and engine components for Airbus, Boeing, Embraer and other aircraft makers, with sites in Spain, the UK, Germany, Brazil, the US, Mexico and India. Employs roughly 5,000 to 6,000 people. Owned by private equity firms led by Cinven. Pure B2B, with no consumer brand awareness.

Alera Group is a Deerfield, Illinois-based insurance brokerage and financial services firm, offering employee benefits, property and casualty, retirement plan, wealth management and consulting services to businesses and individuals through acquired local agencies across the US. Backed by private equity investors, including Stone Point Capital, with growth through frequent acquisitions. Revenue is about $1 billion or more. Mainly B2B, with some local consumer exposure but little national brand awareness.

Alexander & Baldwin is a Honolulu-based real estate investment trust (NYSE: ALEX) focused on Hawaii, which owns commercial real estate, such as shopping centers and industrial properties, and land holdings, including agricultural lands on Maui and Kauai. Its roots go back to 1870 as a sugar and shipping company. Revenue comes from rents and land sales. Listed REIT with strong regional recognition in Hawaii but little national consumer visibility.

Allied Properties REIT is a Toronto-based Canadian real estate investment trust (TSX: AP.UN) that owns and operates urban workspace, mostly historic office conversions and data centre space in downtown Toronto, Montreal, Vancouver, Calgary and Ottawa. Tenants are businesses and technology and creative companies. Revenue is from rents. The funding figure is in Canadian dollars. B2B real estate with limited consumer brand visibility.

American Water Works (American Water) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility in the US by population served, based in Camden, New Jersey and listed on the NYSE (AWK). It supplies water and wastewater services to around 14 million people in about 14 states, plus military-base services. Revenue is regulated utility rates, about $4 billion a year. Utility with strong local recognition but little consumer brand marketing.

Apex Group is a Bermuda-headquartered global fund administration and financial services provider, offering fund administration, depositary, ESG, middle-office, banking and digital solutions to asset managers, private equity and institutional clients. It has offices in dozens of countries, employs over 12,000 people and administers more than $3 trillion in assets. Privately owned and sponsor-backed (Genstar and others), reaching a valuation of several billion dollars. B2B with little consumer awareness.

Asian Paints is India's largest paint company, headquartered in Mumbai and listed on the NSE/BSE. It makes decorative and industrial paints, waterproofing, wood finishes and home décor (Royale, Ace, Tractor, Apcolite brands), and sells through dealers and Beautiful Homes services. Operates in around 15 countries across Asia, Africa and the Middle East, with annual revenue of about INR 340 billion (roughly $4 billion). Founded in 1942. Very widely known consumer brand in India and a longstanding cricket and TV advertiser.

Carlisle Companies is a diversified US manufacturer, headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona (NYSE: CSL), focused on building products, mainly commercial roofing (Carlisle Construction Materials) and weatherproofing for building envelopes. It has sold off other segments to focus on construction. Customers are contractors, builders and building owners; revenue is around $4 to 5 billion. B2B industrial brand with low consumer awareness.

Chinachem Group is a Hong Kong property developer and investor, based in Tsuen Wan, established by Teddy Wang's family's business and later run by the Chinachem Charitable Foundation after founder Nina Wang's death in 2007. It develops and owns residential, office and retail property in Hong Kong and mainland China. Privately held, with funding shown in Hong Kong dollars. Known in Hong Kong's property market and for philanthropy; moderate local brand awareness.

Crown Resorts is an Australian casino and resort operator based in Melbourne, owning Crown Melbourne, Crown Perth and, via Crown Sydney, a large integrated resort at Barangaroo. Customers are domestic and international gamblers, hotel guests and diners. Taken private in 2022 when Blackstone acquired it for about A$8.9 billion, after a damaging money laundering inquiry and regulatory penalties. Well known Australian entertainment brand, with reputational and regulatory issues relevant to sponsorship.

Cryoport provides temperature-controlled logistics for the life sciences industry, including frozen shipping systems for cell and gene therapies, clinical trial materials and biopharma. It is based in Brentwood, Tennessee, and listed on Nasdaq (CYRX), with operations in North America, Europe and Asia. Customers are pharmaceutical, biotech and research organisations; revenue is around $200 million. B2B niche with very low public profile.

Doman Building Materials Group is a Vancouver-based wholesale distributor of building materials, including lumber, treated wood, plywood and specialty products, serving home improvement retailers and contractors across Canada and the US. It merged with CanWel Building Materials Group (TSX: CWX) in 2019 to form a larger Canadian distributor. B2B distribution with no consumer profile.

Douglas Emmett is a Santa Monica-based real estate investment trust (NYSE: DEI), one of the largest owners of office and multifamily properties in Los Angeles and Honolulu, with buildings in Westside areas such as Century City, Beverly Hills and Brentwood. Revenue is rents from office tenants and apartment residents. Founded in 1971, it has a market capitalisation of a few billion dollars. Largely B2B with limited consumer brand awareness.

Douyu TV is a Chinese live-streaming platform focused on video games and esports, based in Wuhan and listed on Nasdaq (DOYU). It generates revenue from virtual gift tipping, advertising and subscriptions, with tens of millions of monthly active users and many popular streamers. Tencent is a significant shareholder. Well known with young Chinese gamers; a plausible partner for esports and entertainment, but mostly known in China.

Eco Material Technologies is a Utah-based producer and distributor of fly ash and other supplementary cementitious materials used to make lower-carbon concrete, sourcing from coal power plants and sold to concrete and cement producers across North America. It is private-equity backed (Charlesbank is among its investors). Customers are construction and building-materials companies. B2B niche with very low public awareness.

Flatiron Realty Capital is a New York-based private commercial real estate lender providing loans against multifamily and other properties, with the funding figure shown reflecting capital raised for lending. It is a financial services provider to real estate owners and operators. Small private firm; the data shows $1 billion raised. B2B finance with no consumer brand visibility.

Grasim Industries is a flagship of India's Aditya Birla Group, headquartered in Mumbai and listed on the NSE/BSE. It is among the world's largest viscose staple fibre producers and a major chlor-alkali, cement-via-UltraTech, and chemicals producer, and has expanded into paints (Birla Opus) and building materials. Operates widely across India with revenue above INR 1 trillion. Group brand highly visible in India, though Grasim itself is industrial and B2B.

Human Interest is a San Francisco-based 401(k) retirement plan provider for small and mid-sized businesses, offering automated administration, payroll integrations and investment access at low cost. Founded in 2015, it has raised several hundred million dollars from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and Wellington, and serves tens of thousands of employers. B2B fintech with low consumer awareness.

Infra.Market is an Indian B2B e-commerce and construction materials platform, based in Thane, Maharashtra, that supplies cement, steel, tiles, plumbing and other building products to contractors and developers, and manufactures its own products such as ready-mix concrete and tiles. Founded in 2016, it became a unicorn, backed by Tiger Global and Nexus; revenue is in the billions of dollars equivalent. B2B brand known in the Indian construction sector, little consumer profile.

JSW Paints is the decorative paints business of India's JSW Group, based in Mumbai, which has expanded into the paint market and acquired Akzo Nobel India (Dulux) in 2025. It sells interior and exterior paints and related products via dealers across India. Funded by the JSW Group, with amount shown in Indian rupees. JSW is already a significant sports sponsor in India, so brand investment appetite is relevant.

K. Hovnanian Enterprises (Hovnanian Homes) is a major US homebuilder, based in Matawan, New Jersey, listed on the NYSE (HOV). It designs and builds single-family homes, townhouses and condominiums in around a dozen states, and offers mortgage and title services to buyers. Founded in 1959 by Kevork Hovnanian and delivering several thousand homes a year, with revenue approaching $3 billion. Regional consumer brand with limited national marketing reach.

Manipal Group is an Indian conglomerate based in Bengaluru, spanning education (Manipal Academy of Higher Education and universities), healthcare (Manipal Hospitals, one of India's largest hospital chains), and other ventures. Hospitals run in around 15 cities with thousands of beds; revenue comes from patients, tuition and related services. Temasek has invested in the healthcare arm. Recognisable consumer brand within India, particularly in education and healthcare.

Meritage Homes is a US homebuilder headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, listed on the NYSE (MTH). It builds and sells entry-level and first move-up single-family homes in about a dozen states across the Southwest, Southeast, Texas and West, delivering roughly 10,000 homes a year, with revenue around $6 billion. Founded in 1985. Known regionally to home buyers; low national consumer brand profile.

Neinor Homes is a Spanish residential developer based in Bilbao, listed on the Madrid stock exchange. It develops and sells new-build homes, mainly in Madrid, Barcelona, the Basque Country and Andalusia, and has built-to-rent business lines. Created in 2014 from Kutxabank's problem real estate assets, with Lone Star as an initial owner before its 2017 IPO. Well known in Spanish property, but a minor consumer brand.

News Corp is a global media and information services company based in New York, controlled by the Murdoch family and listed on Nasdaq (NWSA, NWS). Its holdings include Dow Jones (The Wall Street Journal, Barron's), HarperCollins, News UK (The Times, The Sun), News Corp Australia, REA Group and Foxtel/Fox Sports in Australia. Revenue is about $10 billion a year. Highly recognisable media group with large audiences, open to advertising and sports partnerships.

Paramount (Paramount Construction) appears to be a commercial construction and real estate business in Port Orchard, Washington. The Crunchbase profile shows a slogan about building success from the ground floor up and $900 million funding. There is not enough information to state its scale or ownership. This should not be confused with Paramount Global, the media company. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Red Eléctrica's telecom unit, Redeia Infraestructuras de Telecomunicación, manages the group's telecommunications infrastructure, including fibre optic networks and satellite capacity via Hispasat, and is part of Redeia, the Spanish power transmission operator based in Alcobendas near Madrid. Customers are telecoms and media operators. Parent Redeia is listed on the Madrid stock exchange. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

Regency Centers is a Jacksonville, Florida-based real estate investment trust (NYSE: REG) that owns and operates grocery-anchored shopping centres across the US, with around 400 centres and tenants such as Publix, Kroger and Whole Foods. Revenue is from rent. It has a market capitalisation of roughly $12 billion. B2B landlord with limited consumer brand awareness.

Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners is a Brooklyn-based infrastructure investment firm launched by Alphabet (Google) in 2021 and run by Jonathan Winer, which invests in urban technology infrastructure such as electric vehicle charging, mobility and connectivity. It evolved out of Sidewalk Labs. Investors are institutional and Alphabet-backed funds. Funding shown is $1 billion. B2B investment firm with low consumer visibility.

Swiss Prime Site is a Zug-based Swiss real estate investment company listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (SPSN), owning a large portfolio of commercial properties in prime Swiss locations, including offices and retail, and operating Jelmoli and the Wincasa property management arm. Total property value is around CHF 12 billion. Revenue is from rents and services. B2B landlord with some recognition in Switzerland; limited consumer visibility.

Telenor Fiber is the Norwegian fibre broadband infrastructure business of Telenor, based at Fornebu near Oslo, building and operating fibre access networks that serve households and operators. It was held within Telenor Group, which is listed on Oslo Børs, and has been the subject of ownership changes and investment. Funding is in Norwegian kroner. Parent Telenor is highly visible across Nordic markets, but the fibre unit is infrastructure-focused.

Timbercreek Financial is a Toronto-based non-bank commercial real estate lender, listed on the TSX (TF), which provides short-term first mortgage and structured loans on income-producing properties across Canada. It manages roughly C$2 billion in loans. Part of the Timbercreek asset manager. Financial B2B and an income stock; low consumer awareness.

Transcarent is a San Francisco-based health care platform for employers and health plans, offering a single app for navigation, virtual primary care, second opinions and cost-effective care. It acquired 98point6 and Accolade in 2024, raising over $900 million. Founded in 2020 by Glen Tullman, it sells to self-insured employers. Moderately well known in the US employer benefits market; limited general consumer awareness.

Vertis Infrastructure Trust is an Indian infrastructure investment trust (InvIT) based in Mumbai, which holds infrastructure assets whose cash flows are distributed to unit holders. The funding figure is in Indian rupees. Financial vehicle with no consumer brand profile.

Visionary Group is described as an education and services provider, based in Toronto, with $1 billion shown as total funding on Crunchbase. Its industries include EdTech and education. There is not enough information to describe its products or markets. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

WillScot Holdings (WillScot Mobile Mini) is the largest US and North American provider of modular space and portable storage rentals, based in Phoenix, Arizona after moving from Baltimore, and listed on Nasdaq (WSC). It leases portable offices, classrooms, storage containers and ground-level offices to construction, education, retail and industrial customers, with over 240 branch locations. Revenue is about $2.4 billion. B2B brand visible on construction sites but not a consumer name.

Yellow Corporation, formerly YRC Worldwide, was a Nashville-based less-than-truckload freight carrier operating Yellow, Reddaway and other regional trucking networks. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in August 2023 and ceased operations after union disputes and heavy debt, including a $700 million US government COVID loan. Once one of the largest US trucking companies with about 30,000 employees. Defunct and not a sponsorship prospect.

Yixin Group is a Shanghai-based Chinese fintech and automotive services platform, partnered with Tencent, JD.com and Bitauto, offering car financing, leasing and insurance through its dealer network. Listed in Hong Kong (2858). Customers are car buyers and dealers across China. B2B2C model, with moderate brand awareness among Chinese auto consumers.

4finance is a Riga, Latvia-based online and mobile consumer lender, operating brands such as Vivus, Bondora-like short-term lending products and Zaplo in several European countries. It provides small, short-term loans and instalment credit to consumers, with a history of controversy about high interest rates. Owned by bondholders after restructuring. Consumer-facing in Europe, but a payday-loan reputation limits sponsorship fit.

Energuate is the Guatemalan electricity distribution business serving much of the country outside Guatemala City, formerly part of Unión Fenosa and later owned by Actis and Empresas Públicas de Medellín (EPM). It supplies power to roughly 1.5 to 2 million customers. Also faced community conflicts over service and prices. Regional utility with high local visibility but not a typical sponsor.

G7 is a Beijing-based fleet management and Internet of Things platform for logistics, providing telematics and data services to road freight carriers and shippers in China, with hundreds of thousands of connected vehicles. Backed by investors such as SoftBank and others. B2B technology with limited public brand awareness.

Grindr is a West Hollywood, California-based social networking app for gay, bi, trans and queer people, with about 14 million monthly active users in nearly every country. Revenue comes from subscriptions (Grindr Unlimited) and advertising, at around $345 million per year. Listed on the NYSE (GRND) since a 2022 SPAC merger, controlled by Chinese owners Kunlun then sold to San Vicente Acquisition. Strong niche LGBTQ consumer brand, well known worldwide.

Hanwha Solutions is a South Korean company, part of Hanwha Group, headquartered in Seoul and listed on the Korea Exchange. It operates in renewable energy (Qcells solar modules), chemicals and advanced materials. Qcells has major solar manufacturing in Georgia, USA, and Korea. Revenue is about KRW 13 trillion. Hanwha group is a large sports sponsor in Korea. Industrial brand with growing international visibility.

Heirs Energies is a Lagos-based Nigerian energy company, part of Tony Elumelu's Heirs Holdings, which has oil and gas interests, including OPL 17 and OML 17 and power projects. It describes itself as Africa's largest indigenously owned energy group. Heirs Holdings also owns United Bank for Africa and Transcorp. Moderate profile in Nigeria's business sector, with limited consumer reach.

Kallpa Generación is a Peruvian power generator, based in Lima, and part of the Inkia Energy / Actis-backed group, now owned by Energía del Pacífico, with gas-fired and hydro plants and about 2,500 MW of capacity. It is Peru's largest electricity generator by output. B2B energy company with little brand awareness among consumers.

Knock is a US tech-enabled real estate company, based in Atlanta, helping homeowners buy their next home before selling their current home, using bridge financing, lending and property management. It raised funding of about $765 million, including debt, and has operated in markets such as Atlanta, Dallas and Charlotte. Consumer-facing fintech, but brand awareness is modest outside its markets.

Oman Electricity Transmission Company is the state-owned high-voltage grid operator in Oman, part of Nama Group, responsible for transmission across the main interconnected system. The input shows an unusual Tunisian location, which is likely incorrect. Customers are distributors and generators. B2B utility with no consumer brand profile.

PatPat is a Mountain View, California-based online shopping app focused on clothing and products for babies, kids and moms, with products sourced from China and sold to consumers in the US and Europe. Founded in 2014, it has raised large rounds, including from Sequoia, and reached a valuation of about a billion dollars. Direct-to-consumer, high-volume app; known among families but modest brand prestige.

Silgan Holdings is a Stamford, Connecticut-based manufacturer of rigid packaging for consumer goods, including metal food cans, closures and plastic containers. It is listed on Nasdaq (SLGN) and supplies food, beverage, personal care and household brands, with about 100 plants worldwide and annual revenue around $6 billion. B2B packaging supplier with low consumer visibility.

SiriusPoint is a Bermuda-based global specialty insurance and reinsurance company, listed on the NYSE (SPNT), formed in 2018 from Third Point Re and the 2021 merger with Sirius International. It writes property, casualty, accident and health, and other lines through the Lloyd's and reinsurance markets. Shareholders include CMIG. B2B financial services with low brand visibility.

Ahlstrom is a Helsinki-based global manufacturer of fibre-based materials, formed from the 2017 merger of Ahlstrom and Munksjö and now owned by Finnish and Swedish investors. It makes filtration media, medical fibres, food packaging, industrial and decor papers for customers across many industries. Around 6,000 employees and revenue of about 3 billion euros. B2B brand with low consumer visibility.

Availity is a Jacksonville, Florida-based health information network that connects health plans, hospitals and physicians for real-time eligibility, claims and authorisations. It claims to serve more than a million providers and hundreds of health plans in the US. Founded in 2001 and owned by health plans such as Humana and Blue Cross plans, plus investors like Francisco Partners. B2B health technology, little public brand awareness.

BAC Credomatic is a Central American banking group headquartered in San José, Costa Rica, with operations across Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panama, El Salvador and Mexico. It provides retail and corporate banking, and is a leading credit-card issuer in the region. Owned by the Colombian Grupo Aval since 2010. Well-known consumer brand in Central America, and a sponsor of local sport.

Bersama Digital Infrastructure Asia is a Singapore-based digital infrastructure company that owns telecom towers, fibre and related assets, primarily in Indonesia and Southeast Asia, with the figure shown being in Indonesian rupiah. It leases infrastructure to mobile operators. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand profile.

CoreSite is a Denver-based operator of data centres and interconnection hubs in major US metros such as Los Angeles, Silicon Valley, New York, Chicago and Northern Virginia. It was a listed REIT before being acquired by American Tower for about $10 billion in 2021. Customers are enterprises, cloud providers and networks. B2B brand with little consumer recognition.

Easpring Finland New Materials is a Finnish subsidiary of China's Easpring Material Technology, set up in Kotka for battery cathode materials production for European electric vehicle supply chains. Funding is shown as roughly 514 million. It is a manufacturing project aimed at lithium-ion battery customers. B2B with no consumer brand profile.

Electrica is a Romanian electricity distributor and supplier based in Bucharest, listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange (EL) and London GDRs, supplying power and gas to around three million customers in Transilvania and Muntenia regions. The state retains a significant stake, with Romania's ownership. Local utility with moderate consumer awareness but not a typical sponsor.

Flex LNG is a Bermuda-registered, Oslo and NYSE-listed owner of modern LNG carrier vessels, chartering them to energy majors and traders under long-term contracts. Its fleet is about a dozen to 13 ships. Management sits in Oslo and London. B2B shipping with no consumer profile.

Forto is a Berlin-based digital freight forwarder, founded in 2016 as Freighthub, that offers ocean and air freight via an online platform for companies shipping goods between Asia and Europe. Investors include HV Capital, Bessemer and Hapag-Lloyd; it raised over 500 million dollars. It has several hundred employees. B2B logistics, with modest industry-level awareness.

Fubon Life Vietnam is the Vietnamese arm of Taiwan's Fubon Financial Group, carrying out life insurance activities and distributing through agents and bancassurance. The parent is Taiwan's major financial holding group. The shown location is Hanoi. Consumer-facing insurer, but a small brand in Vietnam compared with local rivals.

Keep is a Beijing-based Chinese mobile fitness app and ecosystem offering online workout classes, training plans, community content, running tracking and fitness equipment and apparel. It has hundreds of millions of registered users and was listed in Hong Kong (3650) in 2022. Revenue from subscriptions, products and advertising. Highly visible among young Chinese fitness consumers and a natural sports-marketing partner.

Kuaikan Manhua is a Beijing-based Chinese online comics platform with a large readership, backed by Tencent, offering original manhua (comics) on a free-and-paid model. Revenue comes from paid chapters, memberships and advertising. Strong with young Chinese readers, and a major distributor of original comics. Known in China only.

Luminor is a Baltic bank headquartered in Vilnius, Estonia and Latvia, formed in 2017 from the Nordea and DNB Baltic operations and acquired by Blackstone, later ownership partially by Blackstone and Bain. It provides retail and corporate banking, serving around 700,000 customers. Brand is visible in the Baltics but limited elsewhere.

Maoyan is a Beijing-based Chinese online movie ticketing and entertainment data platform, listed in Hong Kong (1896), backed by Tencent and Meituan. It sells tickets for cinemas, provides film marketing, data and live-event ticketing services. A leading movie-ticketing app in China with large user numbers. Well-known in China among cinema-goers; little recognition elsewhere.

Mindbody is a Missoula, Montana-based software platform for fitness studios, salons and wellness businesses, offering booking, payments and marketing tools, plus a consumer app for booking classes. Acquired by Vista Equity Partners in 2019 for about $1.9 billion and merged with ClassPass in 2021 to form Playlist. Large base of studios worldwide. B2B2C with significant consumer app use.

Modern Tech is described as a Vietnamese cryptocurrency and blockchain company, based in Ho Chi Minh City, with roughly $660 million in funding shown. It is tied to the Vietnamese Axie Infinity and Sky Mavis ecosystem, though that is not confirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

On Tower Poland is the passive telecom infrastructure company, based in Poznań, that owns and manages towers for Play, the Polish mobile operator, formed when Iliad and others spun off mobile towers. It leases to mobile operators. Funding is shown as 510 million (likely PLN). B2B with no consumer awareness.

POSCO International is a South Korean trading and energy company, based in Incheon and listed on the Korea Exchange, part of POSCO Group. It trades steel, food, mobility parts and energy, and operates the Myanmar gas fields, LNG business and a motor-core business for EV makers. Revenue is about KRW 30 trillion. B2B with moderate corporate brand awareness in Korea.

TPT Global Tech is a San Diego-based small US technology and telecommunications holding company, quoted on the OTC market (TPTW), with media, VoIP and mobile services businesses. Total funding shown is $655 million, which is likely not actual equity raised. A micro-cap with low brand awareness.

Union Pacific is one of the largest US freight railroads, headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska and listed on the NYSE (UNP). It operates about 32,000 route miles across 23 western states, hauling bulk, industrial and intermodal freight, with revenue of around $24 billion and about 30,000 employees. Founded in 1862. B2B brand with high public recognition in the US and a history of sponsorship and community branding.

Zwift is a Long Beach, California-based online fitness platform for indoor cycling and running, where users connect smart trainers to play a virtual world. It has millions of users and runs e-racing, with partnerships including the UCI Cycling Esports World Championships. It has raised about $620 million from investors including Novator and KKR. Subscription revenue. Strong niche brand with endurance athletes.

Alpargatas is a Brazilian footwear company based in São Paulo, owner of the Havaianas flip-flop brand sold in more than 100 countries, plus Osklen and previously Mizuno and Topper. Listed on B3 (ALPA3), controlled by Itaúsa and Cambuhy. Revenue is around R$ 5 billion. Very strong consumer brand, with Havaianas known globally and with a history of sport and lifestyle marketing.

Belden is a St Louis-based manufacturer of signal transmission networking, connectivity and cable products, listed on the NYSE (BDC).
